info.text: Unit 29 — Certifying release to service. Listening, reading, use of English (present perfect passive), and vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again (Handing over a landing-gear job). Why was the old shock strut seal removed?

generalfeedback.text: Jānis says the old seal was unserviceable because it was leaking fluid, so the rectification was needed. A leaking seal is not fit to use and must be replaced.

answer.text: It was unserviceable and leaking fluid.

feedback.text: Correct. It was leaking, so it was unserviceable and had to be changed.

answer.text: It was serviceable but the crew wanted a spare one.

feedback.text: No. The seal was unserviceable; it was not a routine swap.

answer.text: It was the wrong colour for the landing-gear bay.

feedback.text: No. Colour is never mentioned; the seal was leaking.

answer.text: It had already been fitted to another aircraft first.

feedback.text: No. The reason given is a fluid leak, not previous use.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. At the end, one item is still open. What is it, and how is it handled?

generalfeedback.text: The gear-bay light is dead, so Jānis has logged it and it becomes a deferred defect carried under the rules. Everything is written in the technical log before the aircraft is called airworthy.

answer.text: The gear-bay light is dead, logged as a deferred defect.

feedback.text: Correct. A dead light is logged and carried as a deferred defect.

answer.text: The new seal is leaking, so the whole job must be repeated.

feedback.text: No. The functional test passed with no leak from the new seal.

answer.text: The functional test failed, so the gear will not move at all.

feedback.text: No. The test passed and the gear moved freely.

answer.text: The work order was lost, so nothing can be recorded now.

feedback.text: No. The work is recorded in the technical log.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again (An independent inspection on a control run). Decide if this sentence is true or false:

"A control-cable job needs a duplicate inspection carried out by two people."

generalfeedback.text: True. Anna says a control-cable job needs a duplicate inspection by two people: the first person does the work, and the certifying staff does the second, independent check.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct. A critical control is checked by two separate people.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Incorrect. Anna states it needs a duplicate inspection by two people.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 3 again (Justifying the CRS). Decide if this sentence is true or false:

"The minimum equipment list allows the team to defer one reading light, so the aircraft is still airworthy."

generalfeedback.text: True. Elīna checked the MEL, which lets them defer one reading light. With the item deferred and recorded, the aircraft is still serviceable and airworthy for the flight.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct. The MEL permits deferring one reading light.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Incorrect. The MEL does allow this deferral, and the aircraft stays airworthy.

name.text: U29-L5 Dialogue 2 · people for the duplicate inspection

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. How many people are needed for the duplicate inspection? Write the number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: A duplicate inspection needs 2 people — the person who did the work and a separate person who does the independent check. Hearing exact figures in speech is a real listening skill.

feedback.text: Correct — two people.
Listen again: a duplicate inspection is done by two people.

questiontext.text: Listen to the shift-handover voicemail again. Which stand is the A320 parked at? Write the number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: The voicemail opens "the shift-handover message for stand four-two" — stand 42. Catching a spoken figure like a stand number is a practical listening skill on the line.

feedback.text: Correct — stand four-two.
The message says "stand four-two", so the figure is 42.

name.text: U29-L7 Dialogue 1 · jobs in the scope of work

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Jānis states the scope of work: "one seal change, one leak check, and a functional test." How many separate jobs is that in total? Write the number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: The scope of work is 3 jobs: one seal change, one leak check, and one functional test. The scope of work is the exact description of what a pack covers — no more and no less.

feedback.text: Correct — three jobs.
Count them: seal change, leak check, functional test — three.

name.text: U29-R1 Task card · who signs the release

questiontext.text:
Read this task-card extract, then answer.

TASK CARD 27-51-08 — Aileron control cable, tension check.
This is a duplicate-inspection item. Work to approved data (AMM 27-51-08).
Close-up: both the person who did the work and the certifying staff must sign the task card.

According to this card, whose signatures must appear before the work is complete?

generalfeedback.text: The close-up says both the person who did the work and the certifying staff must sign. A duplicate inspection needs two signatures on the task card — one for the work, one for the independent check.

answer.text: The worker and the certifying staff both sign.

feedback.text: Correct. A duplicate inspection needs both signatures.

answer.text: Only the flight crew who reported the original snag.

feedback.text: No. The crew do not sign the maintenance task card.

answer.text: Only the stores clerk who issued the new cable.

feedback.text: No. Stores do not sign off the inspection.

answer.text: Nobody signs, because the aircraft is grounded overnight.

feedback.text: No. The work is not complete until both people sign.

questiontext.text:
Read this simplified MEL entry, then answer.

MEL 33-51 Passenger Reading Lights
Number installed: many. Number required for dispatch: many minus 1.
Remarks: One reading light may be inoperative. Fit a placard. Category C, 10 days.

What does this entry tell the certifying staff?

generalfeedback.text: One reading light may be inoperative for dispatch, provided a placard is fitted and the defect is cleared within 10 days. So a single failed reading light can be deferred and the aircraft still released.

answer.text: One reading light may be deferred with a placard.

feedback.text: Correct. A placard is fitted and the item is cleared within 10 days.

answer.text: Every reading light must work before the aircraft may fly.

feedback.text: No. The entry allows one light to be inoperative.

answer.text: The aircraft is grounded for ten days with any light failure.

feedback.text: No. 10 days is the limit to fix it, not a grounding.

answer.text: The reading lights must all be replaced at the next check.

feedback.text: No. The entry is about dispatch, not scheduled replacement.

name.text: U29-R3 Work order · the traceability label

questiontext.text:
Read this work-order line, then answer.

WORK ORDER 4471 — Fit new shock strut seal.
Part: serviceable, with release note and full traceability back to the maker.

What does "full traceability back to the maker" give the certifying staff?

generalfeedback.text: Traceability is a clear history that shows where a part came from. Full traceability back to the maker proves the new seal is a genuine, serviceable part, which the certifying staff needs before release.

answer.text: Proof of where the part came from.

feedback.text: Correct. Traceability is the documented history of the part.

answer.text: A guarantee that the part will never fail in service.

feedback.text: No. Traceability shows origin; it is not a no-fail guarantee.

answer.text: Permission to skip the functional test on the gear.

feedback.text: No. The functional test is still required.

answer.text: A discount on the price of the replacement seal.

feedback.text: No. Traceability has nothing to do with price.

name.text: U29-R4 CRS statement · basis for release

questiontext.text:
Read this certificate extract, then decide true or false.

"The following work has been carried out to approved data. All task cards have been closed. The independent inspection has been completed and signed off. On this basis, the aircraft is airworthy and is released to service."

"The certificate names the individual mechanic who did each task."

generalfeedback.text: False. A release records what has been done, not who did it. The statement is written impersonally in the present perfect passive ("has been carried out", "have been closed"), so no individual mechanic is named.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Incorrect. The release is impersonal and names no individual worker.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct. It states what was done, in the passive, not who did it.

name.text: U29-R5 Tech log · documentation and release

questiontext.text:
Read this tech log line, then decide true or false.

Deferred defect: left reading light inoperative. MEL 33-51-01. Placard fitted. Documentation: complete. Release: signed.

"Because the documentation is complete and the deferral is recorded, the release can be signed."

generalfeedback.text: True. A release cannot be signed until the documentation is complete. Here the deferral is recorded with its MEL reference and a placard, so the certifying staff can sign the release.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct. Complete documentation is the condition for signing.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Incorrect. With the paperwork complete, the release can be signed.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite in the present perfect passive. Complete the release-style sentence.

Active: "We have replaced the seal." → "The seal ______."

Type the missing verb form (three words).

generalfeedback.text: A singular subject takes has been replaced: has + been + past participle. Never drop "been" and never use the base verb.

answer.text: has been replaced

feedback.text: Correct — has + been + past participle.
Use "has been replaced" — do not drop "been".

questiontext.text:
Rewrite in the present perfect passive. Complete the release-style sentence.

Active: "We have completed all checks." → "All checks ______."

Type the missing verb form (three words).

generalfeedback.text: A plural subject takes have been completed: have + been + past participle. "All checks have been completed" is the model release sentence.

answer.text: have been completed

feedback.text: Correct — have + been + past participle.
Use "have been completed" (plural subject, plus "been").

questiontext.text:
Correct the grammar. One word is missing.

Wrong: "All checks have completed."

Type the one word that must be added, and where it goes — write the corrected two words that replace "have completed".

generalfeedback.text: The passive always needs been: "have been completed". Latvian and Russian have no such helper, so it is easy to lose.

answer.text: have been completed

feedback.text: Correct. Add "been": have been completed.

answer.text: been completed

feedback.text: Correct. The missing word is "been".
Add "been": "have been completed".

name.text: U29-U4 Bank term · safe and fit to fly

questiontext.text:
Write the correct bank term (one word).

The certifying staff must confirm the aircraft is safe and fit to fly. The single word for this is ______.

generalfeedback.text: Airworthy means safe and fit to fly. You say "declare it airworthy".

answer.text: airworthy

feedback.text: Correct — safe and fit to fly.
The term is "airworthy".

name.text: U29-U5 Bank term · the signed document

questiontext.text:
Write the correct bank term.

The signed document that returns the aircraft to flight after maintenance is the ______. (The three-letter short form is CRS.)

generalfeedback.text: The certificate of release to service (CRS) is the signed paper that returns the aircraft to flight. You say "issue the CRS".

answer.text: certificate of release to service

feedback.text: Correct — the CRS.

answer.text: CRS

feedback.text: Correct — the certificate of release to service.
It is the certificate of release to service (CRS).

questiontext.text:
Write the correct bank term (two words).

A two-person check on a critical control system, such as a control cable, is called a ______.

generalfeedback.text: A duplicate inspection is a two-person check on a critical control system. It is a specific kind of independent inspection required on control runs.

answer.text: duplicate inspection

feedback.text: Correct — a two-person check on a critical control.

answer.text: a duplicate inspection

feedback.text: Correct — a two-person check on a critical control.
The term is "duplicate inspection".

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: These five terms are the core release vocabulary: airworthy, certifying staff, deferred defect, traceability, rectification.

answer.text: safe and fit to fly
the licensed person allowed to sign the release
a fault allowed to wait for a set time
a clear history of where a part came from
the work of correcting a fault
a test to show a system works after the job

name.text: U29-V2 Match document to its use

questiontext.text: Match each maintenance document to what you use it for.

generalfeedback.text: Work order = the list of jobs; task card = the steps for one job; technical log = the running record; minimum equipment list = what may be inoperative; aircraft maintenance manual = the approved steps.

answer.text: the document that lists the jobs to be done
the steps for one single job
the running record of faults and actions
the list of items that may be inoperative
the maker's approved steps for the job
a passenger boarding document

questiontext.text: Choose the natural collocation. Which verb goes best with "the certificate of release to service"?

generalfeedback.text: We issue the certificate of release to service — "issue the CRS" is the standard workplace collocation for signing and giving out the release.

answer.text: issue the certificate of release to service

feedback.text: Correct. "Issue the CRS" is the natural collocation.

answer.text: brew the certificate of release to service

feedback.text: No. "Brew" is for drinks, not a certificate.

answer.text: plough the certificate of release to service

feedback.text: No. "Plough" is for a field, not a certificate.

answer.text: polish the certificate of release to service

feedback.text: No. "Polish" is for surfaces, not a document.

questiontext.text: Choose the natural collocation. Which verb goes best with "an independent inspection"?

generalfeedback.text: We carry out an independent inspection — "carry out an inspection" is the standard collocation for doing the check.

answer.text: carry out an independent inspection

feedback.text: Correct. "Carry out an inspection" is the natural collocation.

answer.text: photograph an independent inspection

feedback.text: No. "Photograph" does not collocate with an inspection.

answer.text: refrigerate an independent inspection

feedback.text: No. "Refrigerate" is for food, not an inspection.

answer.text: choreograph an independent inspection

feedback.text: No. "Choreograph" is for dance, not an inspection.
